summary: Timebound AWS STS assume-role with session-tags for DataOps RDS/S3 migration
description:
Issue summary: DataOps cannot complete a scheduled migration which exports production RDS snapshots to S3. Attempting to AssumeRole from the dataops-account into prod-account returns AccessDenied due to IAM condition on session tags.

Impact: Migration jobs are blocked for a single customer migration window; risk of SLA breach for internal migration timeline. No ongoing customer-facing outage, but blocking internal DataOps rollout and delaying follow-up migrations.

Background: We recently tightened cross-account access by adding an IAM condition that requires a specific tag (aws:PrincipalTag/team=ops) to be present on the STS session used to assume the prod role. The DataOps runner tries to assume the role without passing session tags; STS succeeds but resource-level policy denies S3/KMS operations because aws:PrincipalTag is absent in the session context.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From dataops-account, run: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::PROD:role/dataops-prod-access --role-session-name migration-20260310
2) Use temporary credentials to call aws s3 cp or kms:Decrypt against prod S3/RMS resources
3) Observe AccessDenied on PutObject/Decrypt when evaluated against resource policy with Condition: StringEquals: aws:PrincipalTag/team = ops
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed STS returns temporary creds but session tags are not present in the assumed-role session context.
- Resource policies in prod (S3 bucket and KMS key) include Condition on aws:PrincipalTag/team = ops added 2026-03-01 (PR infra#618).
- DataOps runner is an older terraform provisioned GitHub Actions runner that does not call AssumeRole with --tags or TagSpecifications.
- Hypothesis: two remediation paths: 1) update dataops runner to pass session tags; 2) create a short-lived proxy role in dataops-account that adds required tag (max-duration 1h) and is allowed to pass session tags when assuming prod role.
- Security review required for any change that relaxes tag enforcement or adds cross-account proxy roles.
- Suggested immediate workaround: grant a temporary bypass role in prod with stricter least-privilege session policy and short TTL (1h), issued only by oncall IAM team.
comments: Maya Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-10: DataOps migration kicked off and failed during the export step. Error points at missing session tag 'team'. Can we get a temporary path?

Jordan Brooks (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Triage - I can reproduce locally using the dataops runner image. Will reach out to IAM and Security for guidance on a timebound workaround. Logged linked infra PR reference.

Priya Nair (IAM) 2026-03-11: We prefer not to relax resource conditions. Recommended solution: update DataOps runner to call AssumeRole with --tags or use STS session policy. For an immediate window we can emit a scoped 'migration-proxy' role in dataops-account that passes tags and is only allowed AssumeRole into prod with a session duration cap and one-off approval. Need ticketed approval and audit trail.

Jordan Brooks 2026-03-12: Created draft iam-policy and a short-lived terraform change that will provision migration-proxy in dataops-account and a corresponding trust policy in prod with explicit sessionPolicy restricting S3/KMS actions. Posting PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/662
resolution: Triage in progress. Planned next steps: (1) IAM to approve timebound migration-proxy role with strict sessionPolicy and 1h max session duration; (2) DataOps to update runner to emit session tags for future runs; (3) Security to audit the migration run and revoke temporary role after completion. No permanent policy changes proposed.
